El ciclo de tres tiempos es tan universa: The three-beat cycle is so universal that the word “gigahertz” means just that: how many times a second it repeats. What has changed in seventy years is not the cycle, but how many run at once: a modern processor has several units doing different phases of different instructions at the same time, which is called pipelining, and it also guesses where a jump will go before knowing. When it guesses wrong, it throws away what it did and goes back. A famous flaw of 2018, Spectre, consisted in realising that what the machine had done “extra” while guessing left a trace, and that that trace could be read.

El informe que fijó todo esto tiene fech: The report that settled all this is dated June 1945, was signed by John von Neumann alone, and described the EDVAC machine. The awkward detail is that the ideas came from the whole team, J. Presper Eckert and John Mauchly having worked on them earlier, but the draft circulated with a single name and so it stayed: we still say “von Neumann architecture” today. The first machine to execute a program stored in its own memory was the Manchester Baby, on 21 June 1948: it ran seventeen instructions for fifty-two minutes to find the largest divisor of a number. And the idea that a program can be data for another program predates all the machines: it is in Turing's 1936 paper, where the universal machine reads the description of another machine.

Esto no es un detalle de implementación,: This is not an implementation detail, it is the idea. It is called the stored-program architecture, and it has three enormous consequences. The first is that changing program means writing to memory, not rewiring. The second is that a program can treat another program as data, and from that come compilers, the second half of this block. And the third is that if the counter goes astray and lands in a data cell, the machine tries to execute a number that is not an instruction; here that stops with a warning, and in a real computer it is half the security failures you have read about in the newspaper.
